Summary

SFRFsParameters defines the parameterization of Spectral Fault Receptive Fields (SFRFs), including harmonic structure, sideband structure, and center-surround mask configuration. It provides static factory methods for constructing parameter sets using either explicit mask-parameter objects (recommended) or legacy sigma-based specifications.
Key features:
  • Defines an abstract constant property faultTypes for subclasses to specify relevant fault types.
  • Provides a comprehensive collection of constant parameter field names representing core SFRF settings such as order, number of sidebands, harmonics, mask parameters, and inhibition factors.
  • Implements static factory methods to generate validated parameter structs with sensible defaults and input validation.
Designed to be extended by concrete subclasses which define domain-specific fault parameters. This class centralizes parameter handling for SFRF computations, promoting consistency and validation across fault type implementations. By its contract, subclasses must specify their fault types, ensuring structural consistency throughout the processing pipeline.

Description

SFRFsParameters is an abstract base class that defines the common parameter structure used to construct Spectral Fault Receptive Fields (SFRFs). The class provides a unified and validated representation of SFRF parameter sets while delegating the definition of available fault types to concrete subclasses. Each subclass specifies its supported fault modes through an abstract constant property, ensuring that parameter groups remain domain-appropriate. The class standardizes the SFRF parameter fields through a set of constant property names, enabling consistent downstream access, validation, and documentation. These parameters describe the receptive-field configuration in the spectral domain, including order, harmonic and sideband counts, center and surround mask parameterizations, and the inhibitory interaction factor.
SFRFsParameters includes static factory methods that construct parameter structs using named arguments with built-in validation and defaults, supporting both explicit mask-parameter objects (recommended) and legacy sigma-based specifications for backward compatibility. These methods ensure robust and reproducible parameter creation across all subclasses. Figure 1 depicts the static attributes of the class SFRFsParameters.
Figure 1. Abstract class SFRFsParameters.

Static methods

buildSFRFsParameters

Method
Description
buildSFRFsParameters(parameter=value, …)
Recommended. Creates a validated struct of SFRF parameters using name–value arguments with explicit mask-parameter objects (for example centerMask and surroundMask). Provides defaults and argument validation and reflects the current mask-object parameterization model.

Parameters meaning

A formal description of the parameters can be found in Reference [1]. Here we provide a minimal explanation.
Figure 1. Difference of Gaussians (DoG) shape parameters.
Figure 1 depicts a difference of Gaussians (DoG) gain profile obtained from two Gaussian profiles of different sign. The positive Gaussian (green profile) is called the center, the negative Gaussian (red profile) is called the surround. The central frequency of both center and surround coincide with a given characteristic frequency or frequency of interest. DoG can include more than one monitoring frequency by means of specifying the number of harmonics and the number of sidebands.
Figure 2. DoG spectral mask example.
Figure 2 plots the DoG spectral mask for a concrete example. The frequency of interest f corresponds with the Ball Pass Frequency (BPF) of a heavy duty bearing LDK UER204 (see ParametersRollingBearing, and Reference [2]); other parameters correspond with those that are associated with this class and are:
Parameters
Description
numHarmonics
the number of harmonics equals 10
numSidebands
the number of sidebands equals 2
sigmaCenter
the shape parameters for the center denoted as are the bandwith Hz, and the sigma rule
sigmaSurround
the shape parameters for the surround are the bandwith Hz, and the sigma rule
inhibitionFactor
the inhibition factor .
order
the number of stacked SFRFs values, not depicted in the figure (see Reference [1]).

Parameterization of super-Gaussian family

In SFRFs Version 1.0.0, spectral masks were parameterized using Gaussian bandwidth and sigma-rule pairs for center and surround regions. In the generalized formulation, mask parameterization is delegated to mask-parameter objects, allowing different admissible spectral mask families. In particular, super-Gaussian masks are supported as a default generalized form. A super-Gaussian mask is centered at a characteristic frequency and controlled by a scale parameter that determines effective bandwidth and a shape parameter that controls profile sharpness. The Gaussian mask arises as a special case of this family. Increasing the shape parameter yields flatter, more box-like profiles, which can improve robustness under finite spectral resolution and FFT bin misalignment, while lower values produce smoother profiles. This generalized mask parameterization preserves the receptive-field interpretation while relaxing strict Gaussian assumptions and enabling better adaptation to harmonic dispersion and resolution effects. Center and surround receptive field gain functions are constructed independently from their respective mask parameter objects, and contrast is computed only at the response level; consequently, difference-of-Gaussians refers to a contrast mapping between two receptive field responses, not to a single gain function.
Figure 3. Super-Gaussian profiles showing the effect of varying parameter β.

Example

Being abstract we cannot instantiate this class, for a complete example see SFRFsParametersRollingBearings. For the provided example we can nevertheless instantiate a struct descriptor.

Recommended

% Recommended method: buildSFRFsParameters with explicit mask objects
 
% core SFRF settings
order = 3;
numSidebands = 2;
numHarmonics = 10;
 
% center and surround masks
% Note: GaussianMaskParameters and SuperGaussianMaskParameters are examples
% of admissible mask families.
centerMask = GaussianMaskParameters( ...
bandwidth = 4, ...
sigmaRule = 2/3);
 
surroundMask = SuperGaussianMaskParameters( ...
alpha = 2, ...
beta = 100);
 
% inhibition factor
inhibitionFactor = 1/5;
 
% use static method to define the SFRFs parameters
sfrfsParams = SFRFsParameters.buildSFRFsParameters( ...
order = order, ...
numHarmonics = numHarmonics, ...
numSidebands = numSidebands, ...
centerMask = centerMask, ...
surroundMask = surroundMask, ...
inhibitionFactor = inhibitionFactor);
 
disp(sfrfsParams);
order: 3 numSidebands: 2 numHarmonics: 10 centerMask: [1×1 GaussianMaskParameters] surroundMask: [1×1 SuperGaussianMaskParameters] inhibitionFactor: 0.2000

Legacy

% SFRFs order
order = 3;
% number of sidebands
numSidebands = 2;
% number of harmonics
numHarmonics = 10;
% center bandwith (Hz)
centerBandwith = 4;
% center sigma rule
centerSigmaRule = 2/3;
% center shape parameters
sigmaCenter = [centerBandwith,centerSigmaRule];
% center bandwith (Hz)
surroundBandwith = 3*centerBandwith;
% center sigma rule
surroundSigmaRule = 2/3;
% center shape parameters
sigmaSurround = [surroundBandwith,surroundSigmaRule];
% inhibition factor
inhibitionFactor = 1/3;
 
% use static method to define the SFRFs parameters
sfrfsParams = SFRFsParameters.createSFRFsParameters(...
order=order, ...
numHarmonics=numHarmonics, ...
numSidebands=numSidebands, ...
sigmaCenter=sigmaCenter, ...
sigmaSurround=sigmaSurround, ...
inhibitionFactor=inhibitionFactor);
disp(sfrfsParams);
order: 3 numSidebands: 2 numHarmonics: 10 sigmaCenter: [4 0.6667] sigmaSurround: [12 0.6667] centerMask: [1×1 GaussianMaskParameters] surroundMask: [1×1 GaussianMaskParameters] inhibitionFactor: 0.3333
